title: Governance of Student Care Centres and Minimising Disruptions in Event of Abrupt Centre Closures
what_it_is: Governance of Student Care Centres and Minimising Disruptions in Event of Abrupt Centre Closures

sections.label: Minimising disruption to students and families
sections.summary: The first priority was to minimise disruption and ensure students in LPLC-operated SCCs and KCare centres continued receiving after-school care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Our first priority was to minimise the disruption to students and their families, and to ensure that students enrolled in the LPLC-operated SCCs and KCare centres continued to receive care after school.

sections.label: Sourcing new operators and supporting staff
sections.summary: MOE is sourcing new SCC and KCare operators and working with NTUC and the Education Services Union to support affected former LPLC staff.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: MOE has started sourcing for new SCC and KCare operators to provide after-school care for the students in the affected schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: MOE is also concerned about former LPLC staff who have been adversely affected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are working with the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and the Education Services Union, who are supporting affected workers with short-term financial relief, job referrals and career guidance through NTUC’s Employment and Employability Institute (e2i).

sections.label: Reviewing selection and monitoring processes
sections.summary: MOE recognises room for improvement in the sector and is further reviewing its processes for selecting and monitoring SCC and KCare operators.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Nevertheless, we do recognise that there is room for improvement within the sector to provide better services, to strengthen the resilience of operators and to better monitor the service provision.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are further reviewing our processes for selecting and monitoring SCC and KCare operators.

sections.label: Yearly audited financial statements required
sections.summary: Since January 2025, all awarded contracts require a yearly submission of audited financial statements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Since January 2025, all the contracts that have been awarded require then a yearly submission of audited financial statements.

sections.label: Feedback on Little Professors and MOE action
sections.summary: Feedback about Little Professors was nothing untoward, but after a serious February incident MOE acted, and a police report was made over finances.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: As I have explained, the parents can feedback directly to the operator, to the schools and to MOE HQ.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We went back and looked at the complaints or feedback – not all of them were complaints – about Little Professors over the last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Indeed, some of the feedback was about, for example, the quality of food, another child's behaviour to a parent's child, reports on services or the teachers, and we also had a couple of reports from the teachers as employees.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There was nothing untoward in the feedback that we have received from Little Professors and nothing different from what we had seen across other operators.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We did indeed have a serious incident in February of this year, and as soon as that information was made available to MOE, we started to take action.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And we had as our first priority, been stepping in to provide care for the children, and then subsequently, when there were some issues to do with the finances highlighted, we have made a police report and that matter is under investigation.

sections.label: Double GIRO deductions returned
sections.summary: Double GIRO deductions reported before February this year, which happened last year, were returned to parents; a later round required a police report.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The double GIRO deductions that were reported were indeed returned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The double GIRO deductions that were reported to MOE before February this year, that happened last year, were indeed returned to the parents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And so, it is the later round of double deductions which required a police report.

sections.label: Government help coordinating claims
sections.summary: The Government will find ways to assist affected families and parents with coordinating claims rather than having individuals seek out the Small Claims Tribunal.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But given how collective the nature of those who were affected by this are, I wonder if there is some manner in which the Government will assist with coordinating this process of claims, rather than have individuals try to seek out Small Claims Tribunal, especially for parents who are not well-versed in matters of the law.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We will find ways to assist the affected families and parents.

sections.label: MOE staff relieve administrative burdens
sections.summary: MOE HQ staff, parent support groups, former Little Professor staff and external staff stepped in to relieve administrative burdens while an operator is pending appointment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: MOE HQ staff have stepped in to relieve administrative burdens.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I have given the example of parent support groups that have volunteered to assist and we have employed the existing former Little Professor staff, as well as external staff to then come in, in the interim, while we are pending the operator to be appointed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: To ensure that this does not ever happen again, well, those are the issues that we have talked about in the previous supplementary questions: that we are reviewing the sector and we will look to see whether we have mechanisms that we can detect earlier, respond faster and perhaps, have better resilience across the system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But I think the fact that we had such an incident for the first time, a student care operator collapsing in this way, if you like, unable to provide services, and yet across all eight schools, we had a continuity of care and a continuity of service provision – I think it is a testament to the professionalism and capability of our education staff and the entire ecosystem of stakeholders that are involved.
